subject: general
question: A pipe can fill a tank in 9 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 36 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be one-third filled, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Let filling pipe be A and emptying pipe be B.

Time taken to fill the tank completely = (TA × TB) ÷ (TB − TA) = (9 × 36) ÷ (36 − 9) = 324 ÷ 27 = 12 hours.

Time to fill 1/3rd of the tank = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A to fill the tank = 9 hours

Time taken by pipe B to empty the tank = 36 hours

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

Let the total capacity (Total Work) of the tank be the LCM of 9 and 36.

 **Person/Pipe** **Days/Hours** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 Pipe A (Filling) 9 36 4
 Pipe B (Emptying) 36 −1
⇒ Net efficiency of both pipes when opened simultaneously = 4 + (−1) = 3 units/hour

⇒ Required capacity to be filled = 1/3rd of total capacity = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 units

⇒ Time required to fill 1/3rd capacity = Required capacity ÷ Net efficiency

⇒ Time required = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe does positive work (fills the tank) and an outlet pipe does negative work (empties the tank).

Net Work Equation

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in X hours and an outlet pipe empties it in Y hours (where Y > X), the net part filled in 1 hour when both are opened = 1/X − 1/Y.</p
